definition: The MCP SDKs let you build servers and clients for the Model Context Protocol, the open standard for giving AI assistants tools and data.
details: MCP was introduced by Anthropic in November 2024; the official SDKs are maintained in the modelcontextprotocol GitHub organisation.

explainer.lead: How to install MCP SDK, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Anthropic and the Model Context Protocol project.
explainer.inAi: Write a tool once and use it from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP-capable assistants.

tiers.eli5: It's a starter kit for making the plugs that let an AI assistant use outside tools and look things up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the official SDKs, maintained in the modelcontextprotocol GitHub organisation, to implement both server and client sides; a pitfall is that client and server must agree on the protocol, so staying on the official SDKs matters.
tiers.paperLevel: SDKs implementing the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for exposing tools and data to AI assistants, covering both server and client roles.

explainer.example: A team builds an MCP server that exposes a database lookup as a tool and an MCP client that lets an assistant call it.
